# MARKDKBERRY.COM NOTES (April 2026)
# MERGING TWO VIDEO SEGMENTS TOGETHER WITH GREEN FRAMES

This is adapted from IC Union Lora workflow. 

Its for replacing anything in the green frames section of a video using mergegreen lora and depthmap. 

In my case I used it for joining two seperate video clips that were drone shots over a tree canopy. They could not just sit together using Last Frame to First Frame because the drone slowed down at end and starts of clips, which I couldnt prompt to get rid of. So this was my next attempt to resolve it. I took a section from the end of one and start of the next, enough to then green-out the slow down frames. The result I took back into Davinci Resolve to then overlay and conjoin like splicing film with a fix up.

It worked, kind of. The accuracy degrades a little after the Green section but it does replace it based on prompt and prior and latter sections. And... I used trees. Trees are bastards.

I used Davinci Resolve for splicing, and the green frame I made in krita using lora recommended settings but its basically green screen color. 

## THE LORA

- https://huggingface.co/siraxe/MergeGreen_IC-lora_ltx2.3

"set middle frames color to RGB 0,191,0 "

I set it to 0.9 strenght as also recommended by siraxe.




## DEPTH MAP

I used depth map and had to reduce the video to image strenght but it worked even though the green caused a dead zone in the middle of the depth map.

When splicing it back in in DR, the trees at the start of the result matched fairly well, trees in the second half less well but good enough. Trees are a terrible choice so I need to test it with better structure, I think it will work well.

## OTHER CONSIDERATIONS:

Use a FF ref image. I havent tried adding LF or MF in. 

LTX has different sizes aspect ratio to Davinci. so 1920 x 1080 out of LTX will become 1920 x 1024. or is for me. while DR is 1920 x 1080. I didnt want to mess with aspect ratio in DR timelines so just went with what I got.

test at small sizes (work with LTXV: 480 x 277 (16:9) 480 x 208 (2.39:1))

running it smaller than 1920 x 1080 in this workflow will produce worse results (that took 16 mins to complete on my 12GB VRAM GPU, 113 frames at 24fps). I tested at 480 on long edge, then 960, but in DR it was awful, I nearly gave up, then tried 1920 x 1080 and result was much more structurally accurate. 

I didnt try depthmap at 1024 (I used default 512) so that might also help improve accuracy by increasing it. But I also didnt want to trigger a blank zone where the green frames were.

I got banding in result. a slighty blue hue across middle of output one horizontal line, but I think that was tile VAE and so added the non-tile VAE in (its been improved by KJ), I havent tested it yet but put it in place to use next time. Should work fine without falling over to tiling and I can test that issue.
